subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
subtype: Approach: reading the company code of conduct and reporting channel [Action]
passage:
Mentor's note, Friday. Nikita writing about Thomas.
Thomas came to my desk on Monday, troubled by what looked like vendor invoices being approved without receipts. I did not tell Thomas what to think. I pointed to the company's ethics policy and asked Thomas to read it through.
Thomas read all twelve pages, found the private way to report concerns and began a notebook: date, time, which invoice, what was missing, and nothing about anyone's motives.
On Wednesday Thomas used the confidential form. The ethics desk replied the same afternoon, confirming receipt and saying a reviewer had been assigned.
Thomas looked nervous but steady afterwards. The notes were plain enough that the reviewer needed no follow-up questions on the first day.
— Nikita

qa.q: How many pages was the ethics policy?
qa.a: The ethics policy was twelve pages.

qa.q: What was Thomas probably feeling when leaving the desk on Wednesday?
qa.a: Thomas was nervous but steady, having reported through the proper channel with clear notes.

qa.q: What could Thomas do if no further news comes after a few weeks?
qa.a: Thomas could contact the ethics desk to ask for an update, quoting the receipt they sent.

qa.q: What is it like for Nikita to guide Thomas without telling Thomas what to think?
qa.a: Nikita is careful and supportive, holding back opinions and pointing to the policy so Thomas reaches the decision independently.

grounding: The note shows a person reading the ethics policy, finding the confidential reporting route and keeping dated facts so that a report is clear and not emotional.

subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work
subtype: Approach: reading the company code of conduct and reporting channel [Action]
passage:
Wednesday, 14 Feb, 11 p.m.
Couldn't sleep, so I finally opened the company handbook instead of scrolling. Section 7, 'Speak Up'. There's a confidential ethics line, run by an outside firm, and an email for the compliance team. Retaliation is not allowed, it says in bold. Good.
Before I report anything, I want my own notes to be boring and exact. So tonight I wrote:
2 Feb: Bhavna asked me to back-date three delivery receipts. I said no.
7 Feb: saw the same receipts in the system with January dates.
12 Feb: heard her tell a vendor, 'We'll adjust the paperwork.'
No adjectives. No guesses about why.
Tomorrow I'll reread this once, calmly, and then decide whether to use the ethics line.
Lalit

qa.q: What does the handbook say in bold?
Why does Lalit want the notes to be 'boring and exact', and what does that show about Lalit's state?
qa.a: Lalit is anxious enough to lose sleep, but wants the report to be calm and factual rather than driven by upset.

qa.q: What else could Lalit do before using the ethics line?
qa.a: Lalit could keep the notes somewhere private and dated, and read what the policy says happens after a report, so there are no surprises.

qa.q: How might the compliance team see Lalit's notes?
qa.a: Dated, factual entries without guesses are easy to investigate, so the team can check the receipts rather than weigh opinions.

grounding: It shows an employee reading the ethics policy, finding the confidential reporting route and keeping dated factual notes before reporting.

subtopic: Facing an ethical breach at work

passage:
Dolma: can I ask you something work-ish. confidential
Hafsa: always. what happened
Dolma: my supervisor is logging overtime for people who weren't there. I think. I've seen it twice
Hafsa: ok. first, don't confront anyone yet. does your company have a code of conduct?
Dolma: somewhere on the intranet I guess
Hafsa: find it tonight. look for 'reporting concerns' or 'whistleblowing'
Dolma: found it. there's an ethics email and a hotline. 'reports can be anonymous'
Hafsa: good. now write down what you saw. dates, times, what exactly. no opinions
Dolma: 5 March, 9 pm, register shows Mohan present. he was at his cousin's wedding, I saw the photos
Hafsa: that's the kind of note. keep them in a personal notebook, not on the work laptop
Dolma: ok. I feel less crazy now 🙏

qa.q: What did Dolma find in the code of conduct?
qa.a: An ethics email and a hotline, and that reports can be anonymous.

qa.q: How is Dolma feeling at the end of the chat?
qa.a: Dolma feels relieved and steadier 🙏, less alone and less unsure about what was seen.

qa.q: What else could Dolma do before making a report?
qa.a: Dolma could read what the policy says about protecting people who report, and keep adding dated notes for a while.

qa.q: How might Hafsa see this chat?
qa.a: Hafsa is guiding calmly, pointing Dolma to the proper channel and to facts rather than giving an opinion on the supervisor.

grounding: It shows an employee finding the company's ethics policy and confidential reporting route and keeping dated factual notes of what was seen.
